claims.text: An active learning–based approach integrating high-throughput first-principles and thermo-kinetic simulations can rapidly identify refractory HEA compositions that are simultaneously strong, ductile, and low weight.
The starting design space consists of multi-principal refractory elements in various proportions forming disordered alloys.
An iterative active learning framework can refine predictions from high-throughput computational simulations to optimize alloy composition.
Density functional theory and Monte Carlo simulations are suitable components of the proposed high-throughput computational workflow.
Simulations can mimic high-temperature synthesis and ambient mechanical-testing conditions sufficiently to predict practically relevant phases and microstructures.
A dual-phase microstructure consisting of a BCC matrix and strengthened secondary phases can balance strength and ductility.
Tailored nanostructuring can mediate the trade-off between strength and ductility.
Active learning can rapidly navigate the large RHEA compositional space by learning relationships among composition, atomic-level interactions, and thermo-mechanical properties.
Atomic-size mismatch and enthalpy stabilization can enhance strength without sacrificing ductility or low density.
The proposed method can identify synthesizable RHEA compositions with higher yield strength, improved ductility, and lower density than traditional refractory alloys.
Conventional thermo-kinetic analysis and static simulations struggle to efficiently handle the enormous HEA compositional space.
The proposed approach is limited to refractory HEA systems.
The reliability of the proposed approach depends on the fidelity of its high-throughput computational models.
Predicted results may vary with processing conditions and synthesis scale-up.
Real-world synthesis variables and defect structures may alter the predicted alloy performance.
